α, σημαῖνον Πατήρ· τὸ γὰρ ἀβὰ, πατὴρ ἑρμηνεύεται δήπουθεν.
Εἰ δέ γε πάλιν διῃρημένως τὸ δεύτερον τῇ θέσει στοιχεῖον, λέγω δὴ τὸ β, μετὰ
τοῦ συνημμένου καὶ συμπελάζοντος αὐτῷ ρ, διασαφῆσαι θελήσει, πάλιν εὑρήσει
καθ' ὑπερβιβασμὸν ὡσαύτως τοῦ αὐτοῦ α, σημαῖνον Υἱός· τὸ γὰρ βὰρ, υἱὸς
ἑρμηνεύεται δήπουθεν. Εἰ δὲ τὸ τελικὸν στοιχεῖον, λέγω δὴ τὸ μ, μετὰ τοῦ
συνημμένου καὶ συμπελάζοντος αὐτῷ προσαναγνῶναι καὶ διασαφῆσαι βουληθείη,
pass_a_gloss: Completion of the dangling clause: the shifted alpha yields a word for Father, since the syllables aba mean father beyond doubt. Second demonstration: isolating beta, the letter ranked second, along with its attached rho, and shifting that same alpha again, produces a word for Son, since bar means son beyond doubt. Third demonstration begun: the reader is invited to sound out and decode mu, the closing letter, together with whatever sticks to it.
pass_b_english: alpha, a grouping that signifies Father — for ‘aba’ is surely translated father.

And if he should wish to explain separately the second letter in position — I mean beta — together with the rho joined and clinging to it, he will again discover, by likewise carrying over the same alpha, a grouping that signifies Son — for ‘bar’ is surely translated son.
But if he should wish to read in along with it, and to explain, the final letter — I mean mu — together with what is joined and clinging to it,

lemmas.gloss: to read along with, sound out together

choices.choice: The argument turns on the Semitic syllables; English glosses follow each.
Opens lowercase continuing frag-open; closes without a period into frag-rem-mid.
Is surely translated: the particle marks the reading as certain.
